question: A retrieval-augmented pipeline uses Claude's search results feature to ground answers in a custom knowledge base of internal policy documents. The architect wants the final synthesis to retain proper source attribution comparable to what web search citations provide. What does the search results feature primarily enable in this scenario?
options: A) A guarantee that every retrieved passage is the single most recent version of the relevant internal policy document
B) Automatic reconciliation of any conflicting policy statements found across different internal documents in the knowledge base
C) Automatic conversion of all retrieved policy text into a single normalized document format before synthesis begins
D) Natural citations with proper source attribution for the custom knowledge base, similar in quality to web search citations
correct_answers: D) Natural citations with proper source attribution for the custom knowledge base, similar in quality to web search citations
explanations: The feature does not verify recency or guarantee that a retrieved passage is the latest version; that determination still depends on the underlying document metadata.
The feature provides attribution for retrieved content; it does not itself resolve disagreements between conflicting internal documents.
The feature attributes retrieved passages to their sources rather than normalizing or reformatting the underlying documents.
Correct. Search results are designed to enable natural citations with proper source attribution for custom knowledge bases and tools, achieving citation quality comparable to web search.
